[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Samir (Hyperlane - CTO): Samir here. Jules and Leah are with me.
[00:09] Jules (Lead ML Eng): Hey.
[00:11] Leah (Infra): Hi all.
[00:13] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi, Priya from Redwood. We'll cover hybrid retrieval and hosting options.
[00:18] Alex: High level — Hyperlane is looking at improving retail search relevance with a hybrid approach, right? sparse signals + dense rerank?
[00:25] Samir: Yes. We have a BM25-like sparse layer and then we do a dense rerank with embeddings. Right now it's all prototyped with an in-house vector store, but it's flaky at scale.
[00:34] Jules: We get spikes during promotions — QPS goes from 200 to 2k for like 10-15 mins, that causes cold caches to tank and latency to blow up.
[00:42] Priya: Got it. Is your vector DB sharded horizontally? What's your fanout when you do KNN?
[00:46] Jules: We shard by doc id, fanout to 12 shards for topk 100 requests. But we often truncate to topk 10 then rerank.
[00:52] Alex: That fanout is one of the big levers on cost/latency. For hybrid we typically see: sparse layer reduces candidate set maybe to 200-500, then embed and rerank. Are you doing embeddings at query-time or storing precomputed vectors?
[01:02] Jules: Precomputed for docs; queries we embed on the fly. Query embedding latency is about 12-15ms on our CPU pipeline — that part's okay but the vector search across shards is the problem.
[01:12] Leah: Also concerns about PII in some product descriptions, legal flagged some regional residency stuff. So we may need VPC or private-hosted components.
[01:20] Priya: Ok good to know — that will influence Hosted vs Private decisions. A few paths: hosted for ease, dedicated reserved if you want predictable throughput and isolation, private/VPC if you need network isolation or strict residency.
[01:31] Samir: Can Redwood handle hot spikes? Like elastic autoscale that doesn't cost us a ton?
[01:36] Alex: Yes — Dedicated gives predictable baseline with burst options; Hosted auto-scales but you pay for on-demand usage. We can show cost models. Also caching (prefix/KV cache) reduces repeated token or prefix work — though I know you mean vector cache here, but we have prefix KV for generation models. For embeddings we recommend a result-level cache at the vector DB or a small LRU at the edge.
[01:53] Jules: Quick question — dimensionality: we currently use 512 dims for doc vectors. Is 256 or 128 good enough for rerank?
[02:01] Priya: Short answer: depends on your retrieval quality requirements. 128 is cost-efficient and often sufficient with a strong reranker; 256 is a common compromise. We usually recommend benchmarking at 128/256 to see delta in MAP/NDCG for your dataset. Quantization (int8/4-bit) also affects quality — can save 2-4x on storage and throughput.
[02:22] Jules: Do you guys do quantized models on Redwood Hosted? Any fidelity loss?
[02:26] Alex: The runtime supports int8 and 4-bit QAT-style profiles for embeddings generation and vector storage recommendations. We provide model/quant recommendations per workload; sometimes very small loss in semantic similarity for 4-bit but big cost wins. We'll include recommended quant profiles in the docs we send.
[02:41] Samir: About rerank, we're worried about cost — doing a heavy transformer rerank for each query multiplied by peak QPS is scary. Any best practices?
[02:49] Priya: Typical pattern: do a narrow candidate selection first (sparse + approximate vector search) to ~150, generate query embedding, do approximate topk search, then rerank only top 10-20 using a heavier model. Also use caching for hot queries, and TTLs tuned to promotions. Redwood Optimize gives batching recommendations and can suggest whether to push rerank to dedicated nodes.
[03:09] Leah: If we go dedicated, can we reserve GPUs only for rerank and keep embedding generation in hosted?
[03:14] Alex: Yep — routing policies allow splitting by route/model. You can route rerank calls to Dedicated and keep embeddings in Hosted or vice versa. We also support fallback to lighter models if capacity is constrained.
[03:22] Jules: What's the typical tail latency for a rerank pipeline if top10 rerank is on a p4-equivalent GPU?
[03:29] Priya: Ballpark: for a 3B reranker model quantized to int8 you might see 50–120ms per request depending on batching and KV cache hits. With batching we can amortize cost; continuous batching helps at moderate QPS. But tail can spike if there's low batching and high concurrency.
[03:48] Samir: Can you show us some real numbers — like cost per 1k queries at 95th/99th percentiles?
[03:54] Alex: We'll share our cost spreadsheet — it includes per-token / per-embedding cost in Hosted and reserved GPU hourly for Dedicated. We'll run a sample cost compare once we know your QPS distribution.
[04:04] Jules: On the vector DB side — we use open-source vector DB with some custom sharding. How does Redwood integrate? Do you host vectors with Redwood or does Redwood call out to an external VDB?
[04:15] Priya: Both are supported. Common patterns: 1) Keep vectors in your VDB and call Redwood for embeddings + rerank; 2) Offload vector storage to a managed or Redwood-curated store (we have integrations/examples) and let Redwood handle the entire pipeline. Option 1 keeps your existing infra, option 2 reduces operational burden.
[04:32] Leah: If we keep vectors in-house, how do you handle throughput to the VDB? Is there a recommended sharding/fanout strategy?
[04:39] Priya: We usually recommend reducing fanout by 1) using sparse retrieval to prune candidates, 2) using HNSW or IVF+PQ with tuned efSearch parameters, 3) sharding by logical routing (e.g., by vertical/product) to avoid hitting all shards. For promotions, warm your caches or precompute candidate sets.
[04:58] Samir: If we move vector store to Redwood-managed, does data residency become an issue?
[05:02] Alex: For Private deployments we can keep the store in your VPC or on-prem for residency. Hosted will be region-aware but you need to confirm governance. We'll send SOC2 + residency notes.
[05:12] Jules: What's the onboarding time for a private deployment? We have legal that might demand private plane.
[05:17] Priya: Private deployments vary — typical engagements are 6–12 weeks depending on networking, KMS/HSM integration, and any air-gap needs. There's a private control plane option for slower setups.
[05:27] Samir: We have SAML SSO and an internal KMS. Can Redwood integrate?
[05:31] Alex: Yes — SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC, and KMS integrations for key wrapping are common. We'll include a security integration checklist.
[05:39] Jules: One problem we saw: our cold cache performance during high QPS, especially for newly promoted SKUs, is terrible. Any architecture tips?
[05:46] Priya: Pre-warm strategies: increase replication for hot shards, precompute candidate lists for expected promotions, use an edge cache for top-k results, and tune vector DB efSearch to trade off recall/latency. Also you can run a lightweight approximate reranker at the edge to reduce hits to heavy rerankers.
[06:05] Leah: On costs: does Redwood bill per-embedding or per-inference? How granular?
[06:09] Alex: Hosted is usage-based — per-embedding / per-generation token. Dedicated is reserved GPU hourly with unit economics for throughput. There are add-ons for longer retention in Console. We'll put the exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[06:20] Samir: For a pilot — what would you recommend to prove the pattern?
[06:24] Priya: Start with a scoped pilot: 1) Hyperlane shares a 500K doc sample and 2k representative queries, 2) Redwood runs an offline eval at 128/256 dims and quantization profiles, 3) run a lightweight smoke throughput test with your QPS profile on Hosted vs Dedicated routing, 4) measure MAP/NDCG and 95/99 latencies.
[06:46] Jules: That sounds good. How long to get initial eval results?
[06:49] Priya: If you share data early next week we can return an initial evaluation in ~5 business days and a throughput test in 7–10 days.
[06:58] Alex: Let me quickly note next steps — we'll send the security pack and cost modeling doc today, Priya will send benchmark script. Jules — can you share data and a brief doc describing peak patterns?
[07:08] Jules: Yep, I'll upload to the secure bucket.
[07:10] Samir: A note — legal may ask about audit logs and per-request tracing for compliance.
[07:15] Alex: We have per-request tracing and Console retains token-level breakdowns; audit logs are available for Dedicated/Private and as an add-on for Hosted. We'll include the retention options.
[07:24] Leah: Also curious about failover — if dedicated region is down, will you fallback to hosted?
[07:29] Priya: Yes — policy-based routing allows automatic fallback to compatible model variants or to Hosted endpoints to preserve availability; you can tune for cost vs latency.
[07:38] Samir: Ok that's useful. Any gotchas around embedding dimensions + vector DB index parameters?
[07:43] Priya: Yes — index parameters like efConstruction/efSearch and PQ cluster size interact with dimension: lower dims often mean faster distance computations but sometimes require different index config to maintain recall. We'll tune those during the eval.
[07:59] Jules: Anything else we should prepare from our side?
[08:02] Alex: The dataset, QPS profile, and a short list of production queries that are business-critical. Also what your SLOs look like — e.g., 95% under 200ms, 99% under 500ms — that'll guide tradeoffs.
[08:16] Samir: We'll get that over.
[08:18] Alex: Great. Recap and next steps — send security + pricing now, Hyperlane share dataset, Redwood runs benchmark, follow-up session to review findings. Anything else?
[08:29] Jules: No, that covers it. Thanks.
[08:31] Alex: Thanks everyone.
[08:34] END
